attribution.note: Marcus endorses the statement in the coauthored article.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the firm claim that relevant commonsense competence is necessary for reliable real-world agent operation.

contract.note: The contract gives ordinary readings of reliability and common sense, requires separate competence measurements, and allows human oversight without crediting human corrections to the agent. These interpretations matter because Marcus supplied no operational thresholds.

evidence.note: Available before the cutoff. Deployment surveys document constraints and human intervention but do not establish reliable agent operation paired with separate commonsense tests.
Available before the cutoff. Simulated workplace failures illustrate relevant capability gaps but establish neither the real-world antecedent nor universal necessity.

Available before the cutoff. Operational improvement is relevant potential counterevidence, but relative gains establish neither an absolute reliability standard nor absence of relevant commonsense competence.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the packet establishes neither the reliable-operation antecedent nor the contract's conclusive counterexample. Deployment improvements and simulated failures do not settle whether commonsense competence is necessary. The conditional remains unscored.
